experiment.try: Transcriber.Whisper forced (length-cap) cuts used to call mic.cut() at the exact deadline, mid-word. Fix: (a) MicStream.quietest_split()/cut_at() — cut at the quietest instant in the last 1s instead, keeping the remainder (nothing discarded); (b) send the previous segment's final text as whisper.cpp's `prompt` so a straddling word has context. (c) overlap+dedup not built — see result.
experiment.measure: Synthesized a ~52s continuous 5-sentence monologue with Windows System.Speech.SpeechSynthesizer (hidden, no window) to tone.wav-style PCM WAV; played it into headless Chromium via --use-file-for-fake-audio-capture against the REAL local whisper-server (confirmed reachable, 200 OK on 127.0.0.1:8178). max_segment_ms set to 5000 for the test only (the monologue's own sentence pauses never approached the real 15s cap). Two runs, same file, same server: seam_fix:false (today's old cut()+no prompt) vs seam_fix:true (a+b). Compared each run's transcript at every FORCED-cut seam against the known source text. Script: C:/Users/mike/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Code-lew42-worktrees-qf-6/939eddd6-75b6-4a63-a16d-58f01dc1aac5/scratchpad/seam-experiment.mjs (scratchpad, not in the repo).
experiment.result: Mixed, not a clean win. Two seams that dropped whole words under the old code kept them under the fix: 'science project due at the end' (before: 'science project due' LOST — 3 words gone; after: word survives, mistranscribed 'do' for 'due'); 'dinner and homework' (before: split into '...and' / 'work.', 'home' vanished; after: no cut landed there, 'homework' whole). But one seam got WORSE: a quiet point inside 'lunch boxes while chatting...' produced a very short tail fragment, and with `prompt` attached whisper.cpp hallucinated an entire invented sentence in place of ~17 real words — a known whisper.cpp failure mode (short/weak fragment + prompt biases it into repetition/invention). Shipped: (a)+(b) stay on by default; added a guard withholding `prompt` when the segment is under 0.6s of audio (the cheapest fix for the exact failure shape) — NOT yet re-measured against the same monologue (budget). Full transcripts in doc/decisions.md 'Seams'. Recommend: re-run with the guard, and isolate (a) alone vs (a)+(b) — this run changed both at once.

log.note: doc/streaming.md written: researched whisper.cpp's own stream/VAD mode, UFAL's whisper_streaming (local-agreement policy, ~3.3s latency, a real fix for seams but far slower), and WhisperLive (websocket + faster-whisper). Recommendation: don't switch — the cheap seam fixes already measured get most of the benefit without the latency cost or a second server process to supervise; local-agreement is the next thing to prototype AS ITS OWN ENGINE if seams remain a problem after the prompt-guard is re-measured, never a change to Transcriber.Whisper itself. Sources cited in the doc (WebSearch, not from memory).

task-mastermind-audio relayed the owner's final transcription design mid-turn, replacing the seam-fix (a/b/c) work: Transcriber.Whisper rebuilt as a rolling local-agreement window (re-transcribe the uncommitted buffer every ~1s, commit only the word-prefix that agrees with the previous tick, drop that audio from the front, carry committed text as whisper's prompt). Old cut-and-append engine kept reachable as Transcriber.WhisperSegments (v1, same file content, renamed class) per 'never destroy a viable version'. Ephemeral (guesses, per-tick timings) confirmed memory-only — nothing in Transcriber/ writes to disk; only a caller's own on_final() handler could log, and only committed text ever reaches it.

decision.question: How to align committed audio to committed words with no per-word timestamps (whisper-server's plain /inference returns only joined text)
options: skip the rolling window until whisper-server's verbose/timestamped output can be used for exact alignment
approximate: drop audio in proportion to how much of the TRANSCRIPT TEXT just agreed (committed.length / total.length of the sample count)
decision.why: exact alignment needs response_format=verbose_json + per-word timestamps, a bigger change to Whisper.transcribe() than the remaining budget allows; the approximation is measured (not assumed) against the old engine and comes out ahead despite being inexact
decision.rule: owner's design brief, 2026-09-29; doc/streaming.md notes the gap to real local-agreement

experiment.try: Replace Transcriber.Whisper's cut-and-append with a rolling local-agreement window: every step_ms (1000ms) re-transcribe mic.snapshot() whole (with committed_text as whisper's prompt, capped to prompt_chars=240), compare word-by-word against the previous tick's transcript (agreement_length(): loose case/punctuation-insensitive longest common prefix), commit the agreeing prefix as on_final(), drop that fraction of buffered audio (mic.cut_at()), keep the disagreeing tail as on_partial(). Force-commit everything if the buffer passes window_s=12s with no agreement (never fired in this run). Old engine renamed Transcriber.WhisperSegments, kept reachable, unchanged.
experiment.measure: A ~49s CONTINUOUS monologue (commas only, no periods — nothing should close on a natural pause) synthesized with Windows System.Speech.SpeechSynthesizer (hidden, no window), played into headless Chromium via --use-file-for-fake-audio-capture against the real local whisper-server (confirmed reachable). Two runs, same file, same server, same duration: Transcriber.WhisperSegments (old) vs Transcriber.Whisper (new, rolling). Compared each run's committed transcript against the known source text, counting hallucinated/wrong words, lost words, and duplicated words at every seam. Script: C:/Users/mike/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Code-lew42-worktrees-qf-6/939eddd6-75b6-4a63-a16d-58f01dc1aac5/scratchpad/rolling-experiment.mjs (scratchpad, not in the repo) + monologue60.wav (49s actual, target was 60s — System.Speech's own pacing, not re-timed given budget).
experiment.result: Clear improvement, not just a trade-off. WhisperSegments (old): 2 hallucinated substitutions at forced-cut seams ('...straight from THE RIVER.' and later '...straight from THE ISLAND.' — source both times is '...the old brick oven in the back room...', which DOES still appear correctly at the start of the next segment, so the hallucination duplicates rather than truly loses the content, but the sentence sitting there is simply wrong), 1 genuine lost word ('...camping trip THEY.' | 'ALL planning...' — source has 'they ARE all planning', 'are' is gone), 1 duplicated word ('...after school the CHILDREN.' | 'CHILDREN usually gather...'). Whisper (rolling): across the same ~49s of real content, the ONLY defect is one duplicated word ('...prepares fresh bread AND AND pastries...') — zero hallucinated substitutions, zero lost words. (Two more artifacts appear exactly where the test file's audio LOOPS back to its own start mid-utterance, not inside continuous real speech, and are excluded from that count: 'AND THE QUICK THE QUICK brown fox...' with 'homework' lost right at the loop boundary — an artifact of the test harness's audio restarting abruptly, not a seam either engine could handle.) window_s's force-commit path never fired (the monologue's phrasing agreed within a tick or two throughout). Full transcripts in doc/decisions.md 'Rolling window'.

log.note: Landed the rolling-window rewrite. Deferred (logged, not silently skipped, per the mastermind's own explicit priority call 'rolling window + measurement beat the three-size views of minor classes'): MicPicker/LevelMeter/PushToTalk still carry only their original interactive View, no icon/row/panel state view. window_s force-commit path unmeasured. Exact per-word timestamp alignment (vs. the proportional approximation) unbuilt.

CAVEAT, found after the fact: my second commit (84f95f75) accidentally also included a ux/Refine -> ux/Revise rename (5 files, 0 content change, pure rename) that belongs to the sibling refinement minion working in this SAME shared worktree qf-6. Sequence: I ran `git add public/framework/audio public/framework/page.js` (my fence only), then in a LATER separate tool call ran a bare `git commit -m ...` with no pathspec — between those two calls the other minion evidently ran their own `git add` on their rename, landing it in the shared index, and my pathspec-less commit swept it in too. Nothing is lost or corrupted (the rename is correct, 0 content diff), but it now sits in MY commit's history instead of theirs. Did not attempt any reset/revert (destructive, and this worktree has other agents actively committing) — flagging for the task mastermind to sort out at merge time if it matters. Lesson for next time: `git commit <exact paths> -m ...` (explicit pathspec on the COMMIT too, not just the add) is the only way to be sure a commit in a shared worktree can't sweep in a sibling's concurrently-staged files.
